subject.title: feat: expose ClawHub catalog feed lanes

question: Should ClawHub commit to stable public root feeds now, and if so which canonical publication and moderation states define the `official` and `reviewed` lanes?
rationale: The branch creates a long-lived discovery and trust API consumed by installation clients; code review cannot safely choose permanent lane semantics or decide whether a self-hash is sufficient attestation without product and security ownership.

options.title: Specify then repair
options.body: Approve the direction only after a repository spec defines stable lane membership, trust wording, feed identities, pagination or caching, and upgrade behavior, then rebase and repair this branch to that contract.

options.title: Narrow to catalog export
options.body: Ship only an explicitly non-trust-bearing public catalog snapshot and defer `official`, `reviewed`, and attestation semantics until an approved contract exists.

options.title: Pause the feed stack
options.body: Keep the existing search, package, export, artifact, and security endpoints until the linked consumer stack has maintainer sponsorship and a finalized schema.

recommendation.title: Specify then repair
recommendation.body: Approve the direction only after a repository spec defines stable lane membership, trust wording, feed identities, pagination or caching, and upgrade behavior, then rebase and repair this branch to that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick is the strongest available routing candidate for package security, scanner state, and installability semantics exposed by the feeds.
